en: Fine, fine, I get that. [bargaining]But might I propose a very simple solution?
[to himself][under his breath]Rotten bastard...
[dry]Wouldn't you know it? Colin is going to the farm.
[backtracking]Well I would say each case deserves to be decided on its own, uh, merits, don't you think?
Colin stays in my apartment. It's a lot different than a three-foot-tall frog walking the streets.
[pissed]What? If the pig doesn't have to go, I shouldn't either!
Well, might I suggest a path of compassion for the pig? [bargaining]And me and my boy too?
I haven't decided on him, yet. But every situation's different, Toad.
[bargaining]Ah, I see I've given you something to think about. Now let me add another log to that fire...
If you give me one more chance, and hear me out, I see a way for me and me boy to stay.
[pleading]Please, Sheriff. Don't take TJ from the only home he knows.
[very reasonable]I'm not gonna ask for any more than I need. I just want to stay. So whaddya say you just give me enough to cover me glamours, and we'll... [shrugs, giving up]call the rest a wash?
Even if I have to go to the 13th floor!
Just get me what I'm owed.
Then I'll be able to get the whole fam glamoured up.
You're a real friend of the people, Sheriff.
Hey, you've been out of glamour from the word go. I have no choice.
Look, the damages might be a valid complaint, but that's a seperate deal. Weyland Smith can see to that... [pointed]at the Farm.
But... [setting out a possible scenario]you go to the Farm, things cool down here a bit, [noncommittal]maybe you can come back at some point.
Look, you were unglamoured three days ago and you're still unglamoured now. I can't ignore that.
[over his shoulder, to Bigby] I better go break the news to my boy.
I see. Anything for Bluebeard, but old Toad doesn't even draw enough water to merit a response.
Oh, thank you Sheriff! I knew I could count on you to make me whole again. We get this sorted, and I'll be glamoured to the nines, I will.
My future's in your hands, Sheriff. But, of course, I trust you to take care of me and mine.
[overly thankful]So you'll contact me to let me know, yeah?
What do you know about the Crooked Man?
Toad. You help me out here real quick.
Oh, nothing that isn't common knowledge. I'm on the straight and narrow, Sheriff. [to himself]Sometimes I think that's me problem.
[low volume]Look, I'll try to get you that money and get you another chance, but...
[low volume]You have to understand, that's not entirely up to me.
[hesitates - doesn't want to bring it up at first]You've been making it hard for me to trust your judgment, lately.
[defensive]Hey, the fight with Jersey was gonna happen, whether I wanted it to or not.
Nothing is unavoidable, Bigby.
[pointed]Do I need to bring up what you did to Tweedle Dum last night? You are the Sheriff, not an executioner. [appealing to Bigby to understand]What you do has consequences that affect everyone.
You certainly didn't have to torture the Woodsman while he was chained to a chair in the basement.
You certainly didn't have to torture Tweedle Dee while he was chained to a chair in the basement.
It's not just that. I couldn't even rely on you to burn Aunty Greenleaf's glamour tree. And I was right in the room.
So whatever you discuss with them, remember, eventually it's gotta go through me. Understand?
Fine, but it hasn't just been that and you know it.
Toad, this is the Business Office, not a bank.
You're always talking about glamours, and how it's my responsibility. Well what about your responsibility?
Don't try to change the subject on me! I need a little bit o' that walking-around money, you know?
My car... totaled? The gaping maw in my wall? Any of this sound familiar?
Now that we're not in his shop... What more do you know about the Crooked Man?
I figured I'd try my luck with the merchandise here.
Besides...
The Woodsman is broke! You saw the way he was living.
You good-for-nothing piece of... [stops himself before getting really into trouble]
[pointed]I didn't throw myself through your wall! Go ask Woody, if you want payback.
Look, I don't write the checks around here. But I know I had a hand in it[the destruction of property], so... I'll try to get Snow to take care of you.
[pleading]Please do. It's the only way I'll be able to get me glamours.
TJ's been through so much in the past few days...
Sometimes I get the feeling you enjoy toying with people's emotions.
[sarcastic]Gee, thanks. I don't neeed the money for glamours or nothing.
What is this? You bring up the money, get me hopes up, and then give me the silent treatment?
Before we get into any of that, what do you know about the Crooked Man?
I'm not looking for a handout.
But the yolk of responsibility is pretty clealry placed, don't you think?
And you can't deny that.
Now I'm sure you've got your own agenda, Sheriff.
But I've taken a real wallop because of you.
[flippant]I've writen up a bill if you'd like to see it.
[terse]Me and my boy getting shipped off to the Farm is pretty bloody urgent to me.
Look, Crane left us in the lurch, here. We just can't be handing out cash unless it's something, you know, urgent. I wish I could help, but...
I should have taken what you offered back at the Lucky Pawn.
And I even brought in this damn magic coat. I could have sold it, but I know you wanted it.
[frustrated]That's why I was trying to sell the bloody coat! And Jack was getting ready to crack, until you showed up and ruined it.
You know it's not right...
You're going to hide behind some official line?
But you know it's not right, burdening the weakest of us like this.
Of course you are.
This isn't exactly a new problem with you, Toad.
[muttering to himself as he goes]What a crock of shite...
Can I talk to Bluebeard for a minute?
[reluctant]Yes, and a very generous one at that.
Yes, I think we've just about wrapped up here.
Yes, I've just committed to an unscheduled donation.
Did you think Toad would be happy to be sent to the Farm?
[sarcastic]Well, that makes you two for two on the day.
Bluebeard leaves happy. Toad leaves angry. What's wrong with this picture?
Bluebeard didn't just get himself sent up to the Farm.
[calling over]You must be getting soft, Sheriff.
I'm gonna go check on the mirror. I'll be right over there.
Why do I get the feeling I'm not gonna like what you're about to tell me?
[reluctant]Yes, thank you very much for your... generous donation.
[to Snow]Is the matter concluded, Ms. White?
So I imagine this will go very smoothly.
Well, then get on with it.
I'm putting on a fencing demonstration shortly. And now that the Fabletown government is stably funded again, I'd like to be about my day.
I have business to discuss with Miss White.
[frustrated]I think I'll come back when Snow has cleaned out the vermin from her office.
I know you are probably used to shirking your duties...
Did you hear me?
Well, Sheriff?
But I have responsibilities, and I intend to honor them.
That includes keeping this government solvent.
Which pays your salary, might I remind you.
[to Bluebeard]Is everything all right?
[frustrated]I don't have to stand here for this.
[to Snow]You need to teach your animal to behave himself!
[to Toad]Please, you'll have to excuse me...[trails off as she walks off prematurely]
I know what you're thinking, and the answer is "yes." I'm watching you. So don't try to use this little transition for some scheme of yours.
[insulted]What's good for me is good for Fabletown.
You should learn to treat your betters with the appropriate respect.
Why the hell did you burn Crane's stuff, huh? And don't bullshit me, Bufkin was there. I know it was you.
[frustrated]Well, did you find anything tying Crane to the Crooked Man?
[derisive snort]I was simply endeavoring to make the search a speedy one. Surely you of all people can't fault me for getting... overzealous in the process.
Nothing definitive. But that's not exactly what I was looking for.
You beat the shit Flycatcher! And trashed the Tweedle's place for good measure. What were you really doing there?
[innocent]He worked for them, didn't he? I couldn't be sure that he wasn't involved. And I didn't want him interfering.
I see. You're at a loss, so now you're interested in my search.
So what did your search turn up?
A clue that hinted at the witch's identity. But nothing solid enough to act on at the time.
Unfortunately, there was nothing definitive.
You've got a pretty deep rolodex. What do you know about the Crooked Man?
[unimpressed]I expected you'd ask about him.
At least, not without a very expensive spell.
I'm not a mind reader.
Well be more specific.
What's your business with him?
We've met. He's a scratch golfer. But it's always been... casually arranged. [thinking]In fact, if I remember correctly, he just shows up and leaves... very much on his own schedule.
[derisive]He probably mistakes himself for my peer.
Why would I? I'd be surprised if anyone had. You don't become a man of means by tipping your hand at every turn. [derisive]Not that you'd know...
You run in different circles than I do. You ever heard anything about his plans?
If you're waiting me to volunteer information, I simply don't have any. One rarely spills their secrets over a round of golf.
I thought you were going to ask the Magic Mirror. [derisive]If the monkey ever gets it fixed.
Do you know where I can find him?
I'm asking you.
He hasn't invited me over for tea if that's what you're driving at.
Now I really must be off. Some of us have schedules to keep.
Bufkin says he's close. Should be any minute now.
But we're not through here! I need to get---[gets cut off]
[cutting Toad off]Mr. Toad, I'm sure the Sheriff will be happy to discuss this further with you.
Now, I really must get to my business with Miss White.
[calling to Snow][frustrated]Miss White! Are you about ready?
[exasperated sigh]You just couldn't act professional with Bluebeard, could you? Not even for one minute.
[lighlty accusatory]Well how did it go with Toad? Did you take care of it?
[more serious]Did you take care of Toad?
I understand it probably wasn't easy, but it's the right decision. For Fabletown.
It's done. Toad knows he's going to the farm.
How are we supposed to expect people to respect our laws if we don't enforce them?
Look, I gave Toad one more chance. At least while we're after the Crooked Man. [beat]He's had a rough go of it lately.
Then we just don't ship him to the farm. One less thing to worry about.
[accusatory]That's convenient for you to say. [backing off]But we can't pay for anything until we see what kind of a mess Crane's embezzlement left. Bluebeard's donation is only a stopgap measure.
Look, I don't want to tell you how to do your job, but Fabletown owes Toad for how his place got trashed.
I don't think you appreciate how serious a risk that is.
He's out of our hair for now. I think that's reason enough to do it.
It was a calculated risk.
But what if someone sees him?
You didn't fully think this through, did you?
I guess I just thought... with TJ finding the body and all, the kid needed a break.
I like TJ too, but this is something more important. It's the safety and security of all of Fabletown that's at risk.
I think your calculations are off.
I'm surprised you dropped the ball like this.
We all know what it's like to have to leave our homes.
I don't think any of us want to have to do it again anytime soon.
Glamours aren't just something we require willy-nilly.
And yes, I know sending some Fables to the farm is making them leave their homes, but... well, it's for the best for everyone...
You always talk about wanting to do the right thing. Well it just walked out the door. I caused those damages. Have the Business Office pay him what he deserves. It's the right thing to do.
Bigby, I want to but it's not that simple...
Look, I gave him his second chance, and he just walked out the door with it. Next time, he's outta here. Bang, zoom, straight to the Farm. Okay?
[disappointed]That's a pretty cavalier attitude for something like this. I'm surprised at you...
You need to be more careful. Bluebeard's support is vital to having a working government. And he has a... delicate sense of personal dignity.
I know how it looks, but you have to believe me, I said nothing to upset Bluebeard. Really.
[slow, sarcastic]A gentle soul.
Bluebeard loves his theatrics. He blows things out of proportion just to be the center of attention. How many times have you seen it before, huh?
At least you managed to keep things civil between you.
That's not exactly true...[referring to the donation]But as for information, I expected as much.
It shouldn't shock you that Bluebeard provided nothing useful.
Well what exactly is did you do that set him off?
What were you thinking calling out our biggest donor when we're in dire straits like this?
[reluctantly agreeing]Enough. [stern again]And I got a front row seat just now.
We have to treat everyone equally.
[rephrasing]I mean, we need to apply the laws properly.
And if that comes down on some Fables stronger than others, that's unfortunate.
But the Fabletown Charter was written with everyone's best interests in mind.
Do I have to clean up after you again?
If you don't tell me now, it's only going to make things worse.
Someday isn't gonna cut it for Toad.
[deliberately vague]Someday.
I think we need to cut Toad a check. Fabletown has an obligation to pay its debts, and that includes the damages to Toad's building and his car.
While I agree in theory, until we can sort out the mess Crane left us, it's just not possible.
Well when can we.
Besides. He's out of glamour. [sad]He won't be needing his car up at the Farm, anyway.
Bigby drops the shard and Bufkin catches it.
[sarcastic]Penitent to the end.
[side commentary][derisive snort]I'm sure experience has given you that impression.
[gotcha]Wasn't there for what?
I did. Thought that might be worth something.
Good work, Bigby.
That's it. No doubt about it.
Hey! Mirror. Rise and shine.
So[, Sheriff]... care to explain why you let that thief Crane just... stroll off?
Care to explain why you let an admitted
So, are you complicit, or just incompetent?
It's a very strange decision for the Sheriff to make.
